eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecast models indicate daytime highs in Qingdao on May 29 likely peaking in the mid-to-upper 20s Celsius under mostly sunny conditions, with the Yellow Sea’s marine layer providing a moderating influence that typically caps coastal temperatures several degrees below inland Shandong readings. A recent regional thunderstorm brought sharp cooling and gusty winds, resetting local conditions and contributing to the tight clustering of market-implied probabilities around 28–31 °C. Historical May climatology shows average highs near 23 °C with occasional surges above 28 °C when southerly flow strengthens, while ensemble guidance continues to exhibit modest spread due to uncertainty in the exact timing of any warming advection. New China Meteorological Administration and global model updates expected over the next 24–48 hours will refine the outlook ahead of the May 29 resolution window.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from PAGASA place Manila’s daily high near 35°C on May 29, aligning with the month’s climatological peak when average maxima reach 33–34°C amid the transition to the southwest monsoon. Recent model runs and surface observations indicate partly cloudy conditions with isolated afternoon thunderstorms that typically cap peak heating, supporting the 43% market-implied probability for 35°C and 26% for 36°C. No significant tropical cyclone activity or anomalous heat advection has emerged in the past week to alter this outlook. Updated PAGASA guidance and ensemble model runs over the next 48 hours will refine the exact maximum before resolution.
